category: Medical Imaging Toolbox & Bioinformatics Toolbox > DICOM/NIfTI I/O, Volumes, Registration, Sequences, Alignment & Expression Analysis
description: Medical imaging functions for reading DICOM, NIfTI, NRRD and whole-slide images, representing volumes in patient coordinates, PACS connectivity, viewing and registration; and Bioinformatics Toolbox essentials for sequence file I/O, sequence manipulation, pairwise/multiple alignment, phylogenetics, NGS alignment and differential expression.

tools.name: medicalVolume
tools.description: Creates a 3-D medical image volume object holding voxel data together with spatial referencing in patient coordinates (from DICOM series, NIfTI or NRRD files). It keeps orientation, spacing and modality metadata consistent through slicing, resampling and display.
tools.usage:
medVol = medicalVolume(filename)
medVol = medicalVolume(dirname)
medVol = medicalVolume(voxels, R)

parameters.name: filename / dirname
parameters.description: NIfTI/NRRD file, or folder containing a DICOM series.

parameters.name: voxels, R
parameters.description: Numeric volume and medicalref3d spatial referencing object.

tools.example:
medVol = medicalVolume("chestCT/");           % DICOM series folder
medVol.VoxelSpacing
slice = extractSlice(medVol, 60, "transverse");
volshow(medVol)
tools.notes: Requires Medical Imaging Toolbox. Methods: extractSlice, replaceSlice, resample, reposition, sliceLimits, write (NIfTI). medicalImage holds 2-D images and series (e.g. ultrasound, X-ray).

tools.name: medicalImage
tools.description: Creates a 2-D medical image object (single image or multi-frame series such as ultrasound cine loops) with pixel data and DICOM metadata such as pixel spacing and modality.
tools.usage:
medImg = medicalImage(filename)
medImg = medicalImage(pixels)
medImg = medicalImage(pixels, metadata)
tools.notes: implay(medImg) plays multi-frame images; use medicalVolume for 3-D data.

tools.name: medicalref3d
tools.description: Spatial referencing object mapping voxel (intrinsic) coordinates to patient (world) coordinates for 3-D medical volumes, supporting arbitrary oblique orientations via an affine transform.
tools.usage:
R = medicalref3d(volumeSize, tform)
R = medicalref3d(volumeSize, position, spacing, direction)

parameters.name: tform / position, spacing, direction
parameters.description: Intrinsic-to-world affine transform or its components.

tools.notes: Patient coordinate conventions (LPS/RAS) can be changed with updatePatientCoordinateSystem.

tools.name: sliceViewer
tools.description: Opens an interactive slice browser for a 3-D volume (or medicalVolume in patient coordinates) with a slider to step through slices along a chosen direction.
tools.usage:
s = sliceViewer(V)
s = sliceViewer(medVol)
s = sliceViewer(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Available in Image Processing Toolbox for plain arrays; the Medical Imaging Toolbox version adds patient coordinates. volshow renders 3-D.

tools.name: dicomread
tools.description: Reads image pixel data from a DICOM file (single or multi-frame), optionally returning the colormap, alpha channel and overlays.
tools.usage:
X = dicomread(filename)
X = dicomread(info)
[X, cmap, alpha, overlays] = dicomread(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: filename / info
parameters.description: DICOM file or metadata struct from dicominfo.

parameters.name: Frames
parameters.description: Frames to read from multi-frame files.

parameters.name: UseVRHeuristic
parameters.description: Handle noncompliant files with implicit VR issues.

tools.notes: Image Processing Toolbox function. dicomreadVolume reads a whole series into a 4-D array; medicalVolume adds spatial referencing.

tools.name: dicominfo
tools.description: Reads the metadata (header attributes) of a DICOM file into a structure, including patient, study, series and pixel spacing fields.
tools.usage:
info = dicominfo(filename)
info = dicominfo(filename, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Anonymize before sharing with dicomanon. dicomFile (Medical Imaging Toolbox) provides attribute-level editing.

tools.name: dicomwrite
tools.description: Writes image data and metadata to a DICOM file, creating compliant objects such as Secondary Capture, CT or MR images, optionally copying metadata from an existing file.
tools.usage:
dicomwrite(X, filename)
dicomwrite(X, filename, meta)
dicomwrite(X, filename, info, Name=Value)

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: IOD type, e.g. "Secondary Capture Image Storage".

tools.notes: New UIDs are generated unless supplied; see dicomuid.

tools.name: dicomCollection
tools.description: Scans a folder (or DICOMDIR) and returns a table summarizing the DICOM studies and series found, with file lists, sizes and modalities, to select series for reading.
tools.usage:
collection = dicomCollection(source)
collection = dicomCollection(source, IncludeSubfolders=tf)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Folder, DICOMDIR file or single file.

tools.notes: dicomreadVolume(collection, rowName) reads a series as a volume with spatial information.

tools.name: dicomFile
tools.description: Creates an object for processing a DICOM file at the attribute level: query, find, update attributes (including nested sequences) and get pixel data, with better fidelity than struct-based dicominfo.
tools.usage:
dcm = dicomFile(filename)
value = getAttribute(dcm, attributeName)
dcm = updateAttribute(dcm, attributeName, value)
tools.notes: Medical Imaging Toolbox (recent releases). findAttribute locates attributes inside sequences.

tools.name: dicomConnection
tools.description: Establishes a DICOM network connection to a PACS server, supporting C-ECHO (testConnection), C-FIND (dicomquery), C-GET (dicomget) and C-STORE (dicomstore) operations, optionally over TLS.
tools.usage:
dConn = dicomConnection(peerHost, peerPort)
dConn = dicomConnection(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: TLS options
parameters.description: Certificates and keys for secure connections.

tools.notes: Only connect to servers you are authorized to access; patient data must be handled under applicable privacy regulations.

tools.name: niftiread
tools.description: Reads a NIfTI-1 or NIfTI-2 (.nii, .nii.gz, or .hdr/.img pair) image volume, common in neuroimaging research.
tools.usage:
V = niftiread(filename)
V = niftiread(headerfile, imagefile)
V = niftiread(info)

parameters.name: filename / info
parameters.description: NIfTI file or header struct from niftiinfo.

tools.notes: niftiinfo reads the header, niftiwrite writes volumes. Apply info.MultiplicativeScaling/AdditiveOffset for intensity scaling.

tools.name: niftiwrite
tools.description: Writes a volume to a NIfTI file, optionally with header metadata (voxel sizes, orientation) and gzip compression.
tools.usage:
niftiwrite(V, filename)
niftiwrite(V, filename, info)
niftiwrite(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Compressed / Combined / Version
parameters.description: gzip compression, single-file vs. header/image pair, NIfTI1/NIfTI2.

tools.notes: Datatype in the header must match the class of V.

tools.name: nrrdread
tools.description: Reads a volume from an NRRD (Nearly Raw Raster Data) file, a format used by 3D Slicer and other research tools; nrrdinfo returns its metadata.
tools.usage:
V = nrrdread(filename)
V = nrrdread(info)

parameters.name: filename / info
parameters.description: NRRD file or header from nrrdinfo.

tools.notes: nrrdwrite writes NRRD; medicalVolume can also load NRRD with spatial referencing.

tools.name: openslideread
tools.description: Reads regions and resolution levels from whole-slide (digital pathology) images such as SVS, NDPI and MRXS using the OpenSlide library.
tools.usage:
img = openslideread(filename)
img = openslideread(filename, Name=Value)
tools.notes: For block-wise processing of gigapixel images use blockedImage; bioformatsread supports additional microscopy formats.

tools.name: imregmoment
tools.description: Performs fast rigid registration of 2-D or 3-D images (including medicalVolume) by aligning their centers and principal axes of mass (image moments), often used as initialization for intensity-based registration.
tools.usage:
[tform, movingReg] = imregmoment(moving, fixed)
[tform, movingReg] = imregmoment(moving, Rmoving, fixed, Rfixed)
[___] = imregmoment(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: MedianThresholdBitmap
parameters.description: Use median-threshold bitmaps (useful for multimodal data).

tools.notes: Other Medical Imaging Toolbox registration: imregicp (surfaces), imregdeform (deformable), imreggroupwise, and the Medical Registration Estimator app.

tools.name: imregdeform
tools.description: Performs deformable registration of 2-D or 3-D images using a total-variation-regularized method, returning the displacement field and the registered image; suited to multimodal and intra-patient alignment.
tools.usage:
[dispField, movingReg] = imregdeform(moving, fixed)
[___] = imregdeform(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: moving / fixed
parameters.description: Moving and fixed 2-D images or 3-D volumes (same modality or multimodal).

parameters.name: Name=Value
parameters.description: Options controlling grid spacing, pyramid levels, regularization and the similarity measure (see documentation for the release).

tools.example:
[D, reg] = imregdeform(movingCT, fixedCT);
imshowpair(fixedCT(:,:,40), reg(:,:,40))
tools.notes: Initialize with a rigid/affine alignment (imregmoment or imregtform) for large displacements.

tools.name: medicalImageLabeler
tools.description: Opens the Medical Image Labeler app for labeling 2-D images and 3-D volumes (pixel/voxel labels, scene labels) with manual, semi-automated and AI-assisted tools, exporting groundTruthMedical for training segmentation networks.
tools.usage:
medicalImageLabeler
medicalImageLabeler(sessionFile)
tools.example: medicalImageLabeler   % then File > Import > From File (DICOM/NIfTI)
tools.notes: Supports automation algorithms and Segment Anything-based assistance in recent releases.

tools.name: fastaread
tools.description: Reads nucleotide or amino acid sequences from a FASTA file into a structure array (Header, Sequence) or into separate header and sequence outputs.
tools.usage:
FASTAData = fastaread(file)
[Headers, Sequences] = fastaread(file)
___ = fastaread(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: FASTA file, URL or character data.

parameters.name: IgnoreGaps / Blockread / TrimHeaders
parameters.description: Remove gap symbols, read a subset of entries, trim headers at first whitespace.

tools.example:
s = fastaread("pf00002.fa");
numel(s)
s(1).Header
basecount(s(1).Sequence)
tools.notes: fastawrite writes FASTA; fastainfo returns summary info without reading sequences. fastqread reads FASTQ reads with qualities.

tools.name: fastqread
tools.description: Reads sequencing reads, headers and per-base quality strings from a FASTQ file, optionally a block of entries or with trimmed headers.
tools.usage:
FASTQStruct = fastqread(file)
[Headers, Sequences, Qualities] = fastqread(file)
___ = fastqread(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Blockread
parameters.description: Entry index or [first last] range to read.

parameters.name: HeaderOnly / TrimHeaders
parameters.description: Read only headers or trim them.

tools.example:
[h, s, q] = fastqread("SRR005164_1_50.fastq", Blockread=[1 10]);
phred = double(q{1}) - 33;
tools.notes: For large files use BioRead objects (memory-mapped) and seqqcplot for quality control.

tools.name: genbankread
tools.description: Reads a GenBank-formatted file into a structure with accession, definition, features and sequence fields; getgenbank retrieves records directly from NCBI.
tools.usage: GenBankData = genbankread(file)
tools.notes: getgenbank("NM_000520") fetches from the web (network access required). featureview draws feature maps.

tools.name: pdbread
tools.description: Reads a Protein Data Bank (PDB) file into a structure containing header records, sequence, atom coordinates and secondary structure information.
tools.usage:
PDBStruct = pdbread(PDBfile)
PDBStruct = pdbread(PDBfile, ModelNum=n)

parameters.name: ModelNum
parameters.description: Model to read for multi-model structures.

tools.notes: getpdb downloads from the PDB website; pdbwrite writes structures; pdbdistplot and pdbsuperpose analyze structures.

tools.name: nwalign
tools.description: Globally aligns two nucleotide or amino acid sequences with the Needleman-Wunsch dynamic programming algorithm, returning the score, alignment and start positions.
tools.usage:
score = nwalign(seq1, seq2)
[score, alignment, start] = nwalign(seq1, seq2, Name=Value)

parameters.name: ScoringMatrix / GapOpen / ExtendGap
parameters.description: Scoring matrix (e.g. BLOSUM62, NUC44) and gap penalties.

tools.example:
[score, aln] = nwalign("VSPAGMASGYD", "IPGKASYD", ScoringMatrix="pam250");
showalignment(aln)
tools.notes: swalign performs local (Smith-Waterman) alignment; localalign returns suboptimal local alignments.

tools.name: swalign
tools.description: Locally aligns two sequences with the Smith-Waterman algorithm, finding the highest-scoring similar subsequences (e.g. conserved domains).
tools.usage:
score = swalign(seq1, seq2)
[score, alignment, start] = swalign(seq1, seq2, Name=Value)
tools.example:
[s, aln, st] = swalign("ACGTTGACCA", "TTGACG", Alphabet="NT");
showalignment(aln)
tools.notes: For database-scale searches use BLAST (blastncbi, blastplus).

tools.name: multialign
tools.description: Aligns multiple sequences with a progressive method guided by a phylogenetic tree, producing a gapped multiple sequence alignment.
tools.usage:
SeqsMultiAligned = multialign(Seqs)
SeqsMultiAligned = multialign(Seqs, Tree)
SeqsMultiAligned = multialign(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Seqs
parameters.description: Struct array (with Sequence field) or cell array of sequences.

parameters.name: Tree
parameters.description: Guide tree (phytree); computed from pairwise distances if omitted.

tools.notes: seqconsensus, seqprofile and seqlogo summarize alignments; multialignwrite exports ClustalW/MSF formats.

tools.name: seqpdist
tools.description: Computes pairwise distances between sequences (after pairwise alignment or on aligned sequences) using evolutionary models such as Jukes-Cantor, Kimura or p-distance, as input for phylogenetic tree building.
tools.usage:
D = seqpdist(Seqs)
D = seqpdist(Seqs, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Alphabet / PairwiseAlignment / Indels
parameters.description: Alphabet, align pairs first, gap handling.

tools.notes: Returns a vector in pdist format; use squareform for a matrix.

tools.name: seqlinkage
tools.description: Builds a phylogenetic tree (phytree object) from pairwise sequence distances using hierarchical linkage methods such as UPGMA (average) or single/complete linkage.
tools.usage:
PhyloTree = seqlinkage(Dist)
PhyloTree = seqlinkage(Dist, Method)
PhyloTree = seqlinkage(Dist, Method, Names)

parameters.name: Names
parameters.description: Leaf names (or the sequence struct array).

tools.example:
tree = seqlinkage(D, "average", seqs);
view(tree)      % or phytreeviewer(tree)
tools.notes: seqneighjoin builds neighbor-joining trees; phytree methods include reroot, prune, getnewickstr.

tools.name: phytree
tools.description: Creates a phylogenetic tree object from a binary tree topology and branch lengths, supporting visualization, rerooting, pruning, distance computation and Newick export.
tools.usage:
Tree = phytree(B)
Tree = phytree(B, D)
Tree = phytree(B, D, Names)
Tree = phytree(NewickString)
tools.notes: phytreeread reads Newick files; phytreeviewer opens the interactive viewer.

tools.name: nt2aa
tools.description: Translates a nucleotide sequence to an amino acid sequence using a specified genetic code and reading frame, handling alternative start codons.
tools.usage:
SeqAA = nt2aa(SeqNT)
SeqAA = nt2aa(SeqNT, Name=Value)

parameters.name: GeneticCode
parameters.description: Genetic code ID or name (default 1, Standard).

parameters.name: AlternativeStartCodons / ACGTOnly
parameters.description: Start codon handling and ambiguous symbol treatment.

tools.example:
aa = nt2aa("ATGGCTAGCTAA")          % 'MAS*'
aaMito = nt2aa(seqNT, GeneticCode=2);
tools.notes: aa2nt performs back-translation; seqshoworfs finds open reading frames.

tools.name: seqrcomplement
tools.description: Returns the reverse complement of a DNA or RNA sequence, e.g. to obtain the opposite strand for primer design or alignment.
tools.usage: SeqRC = seqrcomplement(SeqNT)

parameters.name: SeqNT
parameters.description: Nucleotide sequence (char, string or struct with Sequence field).

tools.example: seqrcomplement("ATGCAGTC")     % 'GACTGCAT'
tools.notes: seqcomplement and seqreverse compute the individual operations; dna2rna/rna2dna convert alphabets.

tools.name: basecount
tools.description: Counts the nucleotides (A, C, G, T/U and ambiguous symbols) in a sequence, returning a structure; with no output it can display a pie chart of base composition.
tools.usage:
NTStruct = basecount(SeqNT)
NTStruct = basecount(SeqNT, Name=Value)
tools.example:
c = basecount("ACGTTGCAAGC")
gc = (c.G + c.C) / (c.A + c.C + c.G + c.T)
tools.notes: codoncount, dimercount and ntdensity give other composition statistics; oligoprop computes primer properties (Tm, GC content).

tools.name: bowtie2
tools.description: Maps next-generation sequencing reads (FASTQ) to a reference genome index with the Bowtie 2 aligner, writing SAM/BAM output that can be loaded as BioMap objects.
tools.usage:
bowtie2(indexBaseName, reads1, reads2, outputFileName)
bowtie2(___, alignOptions)
[flag, log] = bowtie2(___)

parameters.name: indexBaseName
parameters.description: Base name of index files built with bowtie2build.

parameters.name: reads1 / reads2
parameters.description: FASTQ files for single-end ('' for reads2) or paired-end reads.

tools.notes: Requires the Bowtie 2 Support Package (Linux/macOS). BioMap supports coverage (getBaseCoverage) and featurecount counts reads per annotated feature.

tools.name: mattest
tools.description: Performs two-sample t-tests to evaluate differential expression of genes between two experimental conditions, with optional permutation or bootstrap p-values.
tools.usage:
PValues = mattest(DataX, DataY)
[PValues, TScores, DFs] = mattest(DataX, DataY, Name=Value)

parameters.name: DataX / DataY
parameters.description: Genes-by-samples expression matrices (or DataMatrix) for the two groups.

tools.notes: Adjust for multiple testing with mafdr; visualize with mavolcanoplot; nbintest handles RNA-seq count data.

tools.name: mafdr
tools.description: Estimates false discovery rates for multiple hypothesis testing (Storey's q-values or Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values) from a vector of p-values.
tools.usage:
FDR = mafdr(PValues)
[FDR, Q] = mafdr(PValues)
[___] = mafdr(PValues, Name=Value)

parameters.name: BHFDR
parameters.description: true to return Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values instead of Storey q-values.

parameters.name: Lambda / Method / Showplot
parameters.description: Tuning of pi0 estimation and diagnostic plot.

tools.example:
adj = mafdr(p, BHFDR=true);
numSignificant = nnz(adj < 0.05)
tools.notes: Works on any vector of p-values (not only microarray data).

tools.name: clustergram
tools.description: Creates a clustergram object: a heat map with hierarchical clustering dendrograms on rows and/or columns, commonly used to visualize gene expression patterns.
tools.usage:
CGobj = clustergram(Data)
CGobj = clustergram(Data, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Cluster / RowPDist / ColumnPDist / Linkage
parameters.description: Which dimensions to cluster and distance/linkage settings.

tools.example:
cg = clustergram(expr(1:50, :), RowLabels=genes(1:50), ColumnLabels=samples, ...
    Colormap=redbluecmap, Standardize="row");
tools.notes: HeatMap creates a heat map without clustering; for general tables use MATLAB heatmap.
